summary: The Ieud Hill Church, dedicated to the Nativity of the Virgin, is a Romanian Orthodox church in Ieud Commune, Maramureș County, Romania. Built in the early 17th century, it is one of eight buildings in the wooden churches of Maramureș UNESCO World Heritage Site and is listed as a historic monument by Romania's Ministry of Culture and Religious Affairs. The church takes its name from its hilltop location, distinguishing it from the Ieud Valley Church.
one_line: The Ieud Hill Church is a 17th-century Romanian Orthodox wooden church in Maramureș County, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
key_facts: The Ieud Hill Church is dedicated to the Nativity of the Virgin.

The Ieud Hill Church is listed as a historic monument by the Ministry of Culture and Religious Affairs of Romania.
The Ieud Hill Church gets its name from its location on a hill.
The name Ieud Hill Church distinguishes it from the Ieud Valley Church.
